nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w$, the membership test returns true on $w$ if and only if $w$ belongs to the language of $N$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the NFA membership test

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w$, the membership test is the Boolean that is true exactly when some state reached on $w$ is an accepting state of $N$. The states reached on $w$ are computed from the ε-closure of the start states by, for each letter of $w$ in turn, following the transitions on that letter and taking the ε-closure.
nodes.title: Membership test for encoded NFAs

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a list $S$ of states, the ε-closure of $S$ is a list whose members are exactly the states reachable from some state of $S$ by finitely many ε-moves of $N$ (zero moves included), computed by a search from each state of $S$.
nodes.title: ε-closure of a list of states

nodes.summary: The complement of an encoded DFA $D$ has the same start state and the same transitions as $D$, and its accepting states are those states of $D$ (its start state and the targets of its listed transitions) that $D$ does not accept.
nodes.title: Complement of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: An encoded deterministic finite automaton over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a deterministic finite automaton given as data with natural-number states: a start state in $\mathbb{N}$, a list of accepting states in $\mathbb{N}$, and a list of transitions $((s, a), t)$ with $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \alpha$, read as "on letter $a$, state $s$ moves to $t$".
nodes.title: Encoded DFA

nodes.summary: An encoded NFA over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a nondeterministic finite automaton with ε-moves given as data, with natural numbers as states: a list of start states, a list of accepting states, a list of transitions $((s, a), t)$, meaning that on the letter $a$ the state $s$ may move to $t$, and a list of ε-moves $(s, t)$, meaning that the state $s$ may move to $t$ without reading a letter.
nodes.title: Encoded NFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a state $s$, the ε-successors of $s$ are the list of the targets $t$ of the ε-moves $(s, t)$ of $N$, in the order in which these ε-moves are listed.
nodes.title: ε-successors of a state

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, the ε-move relation holds between states $s$ and $t$ exactly when $(s, t)$ is one of the ε-moves of $N$.
nodes.title: ε-move relation

nodes.summary: The bijection between encoded NFAs over $\alpha$ and quadruples consisting of a list of natural numbers, a list of natural numbers, a list of elements of $(\mathbb{N} \times \alpha) \times \mathbb{N}$ and a list of pairs of natural numbers, which sends an encoded NFA to its start states, accepting states, transitions and ε-moves.
nodes.title: Encoded NFAs as tuples

nodes.summary: Sending an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ to the triple of its start state, its list of accepting states and its list of transitions is an equivalence (a bijection with explicit inverse) between encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ and the set $\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}\,\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}((\mathbb{N} \times \alpha) \times \mathbb{N})$.
nodes.title: Encoded DFAs as triples

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be an encoded NFA and $w$ a word. If $u$ is one of the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ can be in after reading $w$, and $N$ has an ε-move from $u$ to $v$, then $v$ is also one of these states.
nodes.title: The states reached on a word are closed under ε-moves

nodes.summary: An NFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded NFA with the same language.
nodes.title: Every finite NFA has an encoding

nodes.summary: An `εNFA` over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded NFA with the same language.
nodes.title: Every finite ε-NFA has an encoding

nodes.summary: A DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded DFA with the same language.
nodes.title: Every finite DFA has an encoding

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, the emptiness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when no state in the list of reachable states of $N$ is an accepting state of $N$; the reachable states are those reachable from a start state of $N$ by zero or more moves, each a transition on some letter or an ε-move.
nodes.title: Emptiness test for encoded NFAs

nodes.summary: The language of an encoded NFA $N$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is the language accepted by the ε-NFA that $N$ denotes, whose states are the natural numbers: the words $w$ over $\alpha$ such that some accepting state of $N$ is among the states reached on $w$ from the start states of $N$, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.
nodes.title: Language of an encoded NFA

nodes.summary: The language of an encoded DFA $D$ is the set of words $w$ such that the state reached by running $D$ on $w$ from its start state, following its transition function, is one of its accepting states.
nodes.title: Language of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a list $S$ of states and a letter $a$, the letter step lists the target $t$ of every transition $((s, a), t)$ of $N$ with $s \in S$, in the order of the transition list of $N$, without taking the ε-closure.
nodes.title: Letter step of an encoded NFA

nodes.summary: The letters of an encoded DFA $D$ form the list of the letters $a$ of its listed transitions $((s, a), t)$, in the order the transitions are listed.
nodes.title: Letters of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a set $X$ of natural numbers and a natural number $t$, $t$ lies in the ε-closure of $X$ in the ε-NFA that $N$ denotes if and only if $t$ is reachable from some $u \in X$ by a sequence of zero or more ε-moves of $N$.
nodes.title: The ε-closure is reachability along ε-moves

nodes.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$ and every word $w$, the complement of $D$ accepts $w$ if and only if $D$ does not accept $w$.
nodes.title: The complement DFA accepts the complement language

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a natural number $t$, $t$ is among the reachable states of $N$ if and only if there is a word $w$ such that $t$ is among the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ reaches on $w$ from its start states, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.
nodes.title: The reachable states are those some word can lead to

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a word $w$ and a natural number $t$, $t$ is among the states in the run of $N$ on $w$ if and only if $t$ is among the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ reaches on $w$ from its start states, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.
nodes.title: The run of an encoded NFA agrees with ε-NFA evaluation

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a state $s$, this is the list of the targets $t$ of the transitions $((s, a), t)$ of $N$ on any letter $a$, followed by the targets $t$ of the ε-moves $(s, t)$ of $N$, each in the order of the corresponding list of $N$.
nodes.title: Successors of a state in an encoded NFA

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding and decidable equality, and encode encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ through their start state, accepting states and transitions. The map sending an encoded DFA $D$ and a word $w$ over $\alpha$ to the state reached by running $D$ on $w$ from its start state is primitive recursive.
nodes.title: Running an encoded DFA is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding, and encode encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ through their start state, accepting states and transitions. The map sending a triple $(s, F, T)$, where $s \in \mathbb{N}$, $F$ is a list of natural numbers and $T$ is a list of pairs $((q, a), t)$ with $q, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \alpha$, to the encoded DFA over $\alpha$ with start state $s$, accepting…
nodes.title: Assembling an encoded DFA is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding and decidable equality, and encode encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ through their start state, accepting states and transitions. The map sending an encoded DFA $D$ over $\alpha$, a state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and a letter $a \in \alpha$ to the state that $D$ moves to from $s$ on $a$ (the target of the first transition listed for $(s, a)$, or $s$ if there is…
nodes.title: The transition function of encoded DFAs is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, this is the list, found by a search from each start state of $N$ in turn through the start states of $N$ and the targets of its transitions and ε-moves, of the states reachable from a start state of $N$ by zero or more moves, each a transition of $N$ on some letter or an ε-move of $N$.
nodes.title: Reachable states of an encoded NFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w = a_1 \cdots a_n$, the run of $N$ on $w$ is the list of states obtained by starting from the ε-closure of the start states of $N$ and, for each letter $a_i$ in turn, taking the letter step on $a_i$ and then the ε-closure.
nodes.title: Run of an encoded NFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, this is the list of the start states of $N$, followed by the targets $t$ of its transitions $((s, a), t)$, followed by the targets $t$ of its ε-moves $(s, t)$.
nodes.title: States an encoded NFA mentions as start states or targets

nodes.summary: The states of an encoded DFA $D$ form the list consisting of its start state followed by the targets of its listed transitions, in the order they are listed.
nodes.title: States of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, let $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$ be states and let $a$ be a letter. If $D$ lists at least one transition from $s$ on $a$, and every transition listed from $s$ on $a$ has target $t$, then the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $t$.
nodes.title: A step determined by its listed transitions

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $s \in \mathbb{N}$ a state and $a$ a letter. If $D$ lists no transition from $s$ on $a$, then the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $s$.
nodes.title: Unlisted transitions fix the state

nodes.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a list $S$ of states and a letter $a$, the list of states reached from $S$ on $a$: the ε-closure, computed as a list, of the list of states $t$ such that $((s, a), t)$ is a transition of $N$ for some $s$ in $S$.
nodes.title: One step of an encoded NFA on a list of states

nodes.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$, state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and letter $a$, the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ either to the target of some listed transition of $D$ or to $s$ itself.
nodes.title: Where a step can lead

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $s$ be one of its states, that is, its start state or the target of one of its listed transitions. Then for every letter $a$ the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to one of the states of $D$.
nodes.title: The listed states are closed under transitions

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $a$ be a letter that is not among the letters of $D$, that is, no listed transition of $D$ is labelled $a$. Then for every state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $s$.
nodes.title: Letters without listed transitions fix every state

nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$, a state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and a letter $a$, the step of $D$ from $s$ on $a$ is the target of the first transition that $D$ lists from $s$ on $a$, or $s$ itself when $D$ lists no such transition.
nodes.title: Transition function of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded NFA $N$ (with ε-moves) over $\alpha$ that its language is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $E_{\mathrm{NFA}}$.
nodes.title: Emptiness of NFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(N, w)$, where $N$ is an encoded NFA (with ε-moves) over $\alpha$ and $w$ is a word over $\alpha$, that $w$ is in the language of $N$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is Sipser, Theorem 4.2: the problem $A_{\mathrm{NFA}}$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Membership for NFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: An encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ denotes the deterministic automaton over $\alpha$ with state set $\mathbb{N}$ whose start state is the start state of $D$, whose transition function is the transition function of $D$, and whose accepting states are the states in the accepting list of $D$.
nodes.title: The automaton denoted by an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: An encoded NFA $N$ over $\alpha$ denotes the ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with state set $\mathbb{N}$ whose start states are the start states listed in $N$, whose accepting states are the accepting states listed in $N$, and in which a state $s$ may move to $t$ on a letter $a$ exactly when $((s, a), t)$ is a transition of $N$, and without reading a letter exactly when $(s, t)$ is an ε-move of $N$.
nodes.title: The ε-NFA of an encoded NFA
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
